newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines asked to withdraw sugar discount.
newsitem.headline: Philippines asked to withdraw sugar discount.

text.p: Philippine sugar planters and millers asked the government on Thursday to defer its proposed reduction in sugar import tariffs starting July 1 next year, government and private sector officials said on Thursday.
They also asked the government to withdraw the 35 percent tariff rebate given by the Philippines to imported refined sugar coming from neighbouring Southeast Asian countries.

"The twin proposals were submitted by sugar planters and leaders in a meeting with Executive Secretary Ruben Torres and Sugar Regulatory Administration (SRA) head Wilson Gamboa," an SRA official said.
Torres is head of a multi-sectoral committee formed by President Fidel Ramos to map out measures to solve the country's sugar glut due to a surge in cheap imported sugar.

Philippine sugar planters and millers said the proposed tariff reduction on imported sugar, and the rebate given to neighbouring countries, would make locally grown sugar uncompetitive in terms of prices.
The Philippines has adopted a two-tier tax system on imported sugar.

For this year, the Philippines slapped a 50 percent tariff on its first 45,000 tonnes of sugar imports as part of its commitment to the World Trade Organisation, an official in a Philippine sugar mill who declined to be identified said.
A 100 percent tariff has been set for succeeding imports.
The government has planned to cut the tariffs to a blanket 80 percent from July.
Gamboa blamed the import of some 1.2 million tonnes of sugar between September 1995 and July this year for the local sugar crisis.
He had said Thursday's meeting was to have decided on exporting surplus sugar stocks but SRA officials said a final decision will be made at a later date.
